claims.text: Dynamic behavior in solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn arises from a temperature-dependent crossover between thermally activated dislocation glide and dynamic solute pinning.
Local lattice distortions modulate thermally activated dislocation glide in FeNiCrMn.
At cryogenic temperatures, reduced phonon damping allows dislocation inertia to dominate.
Dominant dislocation inertia at cryogenic temperatures elevates the yield stress.
At elevated temperatures, enhanced solute diffusivity produces elastic pinning of dislocations.
Dynamic solute pinning at elevated temperatures causes Portevin–Le Chatelier-type serrated flow.
Cr-related distortions, with contributions from Mn and Fe, are the primary compositional contributors to the proposed elevated-temperature pinning.
The controlled study uses homogenized, water-quenched, equiatomic, single-phase FCC FeNiCrMn with a uniform microstructure.
The proposed intervention is uniaxial compression over cryogenic through elevated temperatures with controlled strain-rate jumps, supplemented by TEM and DFT.
Local lattice distortions create heterogeneous landscapes of resistance to dislocation glide.
Below room temperature, dislocation motion largely follows thermally activated glide over local obstacles determined by lattice distortion.
Below approximately 77 K, significant dislocation inertia produces a plateau or reduced gradient in the increase of CRSS.
Above approximately 673 K, enhanced atomic mobility permits transient solute atmospheres to form around and pin dislocations.
Relative to room temperature, CRSS will rise steeply at cryogenic temperatures and show a reduced temperature gradient below approximately 77 K.
At 673–1273 K, FeNiCrMn will exhibit a modest CRSS increase accompanied by PL-type stress–strain serrations.
The extrapolated 0 K CRSS will positively correlate with DFT-calculated mean-square atomic displacement, with larger MSAD corresponding to greater glide resistance.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to homogenized, water-quenched, single-phase FCC FeNiCrMn tested in compression along a fixed orientation.
Significant microsegregation, secondary phases, or pre-existing defect states may obscure the proposed dislocation dynamics and place the material outside the hypothesis boundary.
Transition temperatures may vary because of compositional and magnetic differences between FeNiCrMn and Co-containing alloys.
Magnetic ordering may influence dislocation behavior in FeNiCrMn.
